feed.title: Mathematics — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: abstractmath.org
entry.summary: A resource opening the places people get stuck moving into abstract mathematics — reading definitions, the language of proof, notation. Unlike topic books it targets how mathematics is thought.

entry.title: Art of Problem Solving
entry.summary: Olympiad-level competition-math courses and a forum community.

entry.title: Awesome Math
entry.summary: A list organising mathematics resources by branch (algebra, analysis, topology). Unlike a single course it maps out where to start.

entry.title: BetterExplained
entry.summary: A set of essays explaining maths by intuition rather than memorisation — exponentials, Euler’s formula, calculus. Unlike formal treatments it answers “why is it like this” with analogy and pictures.

entry.title: Desmos
entry.summary: A free online graphing calculator producing fast, shareable interactive graphs.

entry.title: Encyclopedia of Mathematics
entry.summary: An EMS/Springer-backed maths wiki of authoritative survey articles.

entry.title: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra (UBC)
entry.summary: A free UBC text building linear algebra from the ground up. Unlike short notes it is a complete, proof-carrying resource for those who want the reasoning behind the course.

entry.title: GeoGebra
entry.summary: Dynamic maths software that links geometry, algebra and calculus live.

entry.title: Interactive Mathematics
entry.summary: A site teaching mathematics topic by topic with interactive graphs and worked examples. Unlike static notes you can move the graph in place and see the result.

entry.title: Math ∩ Programming
entry.summary: Jeremy Kun’s blog joining mathematics with working code — cryptography, graphs, the maths of machine learning. Unlike pure theory it closes each concept with an implementation.

entry.title: math-as-code
entry.summary: A cheat sheet mapping mathematical notation to readable code: sigma sums, dot products. Unlike symbol glossaries it shows what the formula means to a programmer.

entry.title: Math3ma
entry.summary: An approachable graduate-maths blog that builds intuition for abstract topics.

entry.title: Mathematics Stack Exchange
entry.summary: A mathematics Q&A site where you can ask experts about the step you are stuck on. Unlike a forum, voting surfaces the clearest solution.

entry.title: Mathigon
entry.summary: An interactive maths textbook with manipulable, story-driven lessons.

entry.title: MathOverflow
entry.summary: A high-rigour question-and-answer site for research mathematicians.

entry.title: MIT · Mathematics for Computer Science
entry.summary: An MIT course gathering the discrete mathematics a computer scientist needs — logic, counting, graphs, probability — in one place. Unlike general maths courses it aims straight at CS.

entry.title: OEIS
entry.summary: The Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences — look any sequence up by its terms.

entry.title: OpenIntro Statistics
entry.summary: A free, open textbook for introductory statistics, covering data, inference and regression by example. Unlike commercial texts it is free and comes with exercises and slides.

entry.title: Paul’s Online Math Notes
entry.summary: Clean, worked lecture notes for algebra, calculus and differential equations (Lamar University). Unlike a textbook it is ideal for a quick refresh before an exam.

entry.title: Probability Cheatsheet
entry.summary: A cheat sheet compressing a probability course’s distributions, expectations and theorems onto one page. Unlike a textbook it can be scanned at a glance during an exam.

entry.title: ProofWiki
entry.summary: A collaborative maths database holding proofs, not just statements.

entry.title: Seeing Theory
entry.summary: A Brown University project teaching probability and statistics entirely through interactive visuals. Unlike a textbook you see the concept by dragging and trying — you move the distribution by hand.

entry.title: Stanford CS229 · Linear Algebra Review
entry.summary: A Stanford reference summarising the linear algebra needed for machine learning. Unlike a full course it is a quick refresher focused only on the parts ML uses.

entry.title: Symbolab
entry.summary: An equation solver that shows the worked steps to a solution.

entry.title: Wolfram MathWorld
entry.summary: An extensive, rigorous and cross-linked mathematics encyclopedia.

entry.title: 3Blue1Brown
entry.summary: Grant Sanderson’s channel and site explaining mathematics through animation — linear algebra, calculus, analysis. Unlike lectures it shows the picture behind the formula, not just the formula.

entry.title: Graph Online
entry.summary: Draw a graph in the browser and run shortest path, connectivity and flow algorithms on it — testing graph algorithms without writing code.

entry.title: Khan Academy · Matematik
entry.summary: A free platform teaching mathematics from primary school to university, with exercises in order. Unlike scattered videos it offers a full curriculum that builds on prior topics.

entry.title: Manim Community
entry.summary: The community edition of the Python library behind the mathematical animations in 3Blue1Brown videos; you describe the scene in code. Unlike general animation tools it treats equations, graphs and transformations as first-class objects.
